- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 2–3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.40) and model is flat or declining, force a slight upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.5% per day) to align with sentiment.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 10–15 days of price action shows strong trend, add 0.5–1.0% upward correction for remaining days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.20–0.35), model often lags; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by shifting forecast up 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid premature reversal.
